assign.title: The event log, the projections, the naming rules, and the conflict rule
assign.request: Design the log and content model for the Servex Mastermind: one append-only JSONL per session of typed immutable events; tasks, decisions, proposals and prompts folded from events, never edited in place; the prompt lifecycle raw -> refined -> pre-proposal -> proposal -> build; the naming rules as checks the appender enforces; a recommendation on conflict handling; and the assistant tiers. Design only, no server code. Brief: ai/2026-09-22/log-model/requirements.md

log.msg: fold.js proven over sample.jsonl in node: 30 of 30 lines parsed, 0 orphans, and every rule holds - the owner's rename applied, the approve locked the name, three alternatives were kept beside it, the newest intent became the task's now, the decision read approved, and the proposal advanced from pre to full. Prover script is in the scratchpad (log-model-prove.mjs).

decision.about: In {at, id, type, by}, is id the line's own address or the id of the thing the line is about?

options.say: id names the THING; a separate seq addresses the line
options.why: Matches how today's log already merges ask, decision, agent and note by id, so nothing on the board is orphaned, and it makes re: point at something a person can name.

options.say: id is the line's own unique id
options.why: Simpler to mint, but then every reference points at a line number nobody can read, and grouping needs a second key per type anyway.

decision.because: The owner's own fold rule says 'the newest task event per id', which only means anything if id names the task.

decision.about: How does a refined event cite the raw prompt it came from - character offsets or sentence index?

options.say: Sentence index into an array the prompt event itself stores
options.why: The split happens once, at write time, and is part of the immutable event - so an index can never drift, and a person can check 'sentences 0 and 2' by reading them.

options.say: Character offsets into the raw text
options.why: Exact to the character, but a re-transcription that fixes one word shifts every offset after it and silently breaks every citation.

decision.because: Dictated text gets re-transcribed; an index into a stored array survives that, a character offset does not.

decision.about: When two agents name the same thing, which name does the owner see?

options.say: The FIRST name wins; later ones are alternatives
options.why: It is the one rule that makes 'the fast assistant names at once' true, and it closes the race where a second agent silently displaces a name before anyone saw it.

options.say: Newest wins, like every other merge
options.why: One rule instead of two, but a mastermind appending a second later name then overwrites what the owner is already looking at - exactly what the naming rules forbid.

decision.because: It is the only exception to newest-wins, and without it two agents naming the same thing in the same second silently overwrite each other.

log.msg: Deliverable 6 (the tiers) came out as a four-row table rather than the three the brief named: minions are the fourth tier and they write most of the lines in the file, so leaving them out would have left the biggest writer unregulated. The fast assistant, the masterminds and the owner are all there with their own rows.

assign.outcome:
**Append and fold, with one visibility rule built into the writer — that is the conflict rule, and the log schema that makes it work is designed and shown running.**

Every session writes one file that only ever grows. Nothing is edited in place: approving, renaming and disagreeing are all just new lines, and your tasks, names, decisions and own words are rebuilt from those lines every time a page loads. Your four naming rules are not advice in a skill an agent can forget — they are four checks in the one function that appends to the file, and that function is the only way in, so no agent can get around them.

[**The log model**](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/) is the one page: the recommendation and the naming checks above the fold, the twenty-four kinds of line and who may write what below it.

![](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/shot.png)

- [**The fold, run live**](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/fold/) — the real function, run in your browser over a thirty-line sample log, with each rule shown beside what the sample proves about it.
- [**From what you said to what got built**](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/lifecycle/) — one thread through all five stages, citations resolved live so you can check each one against the sentence it claims.
- [events.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/events.md) — the full schema, and how every line already on your board maps onto it, so nothing is orphaned.
- [sample.jsonl](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/sample.jsonl) · [fold.js](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/fold.js)

The sample log found one real hole in plain append-and-fold, and it is fixed rather than parked: names are the single exception to newest-wins. The first name for a thing is the one you see, because otherwise two agents naming the same thing seconds apart would silently swap what is on your screen.

Left for the owner: nothing is waiting on you. Left deliberately: no server code — the appender that enforces these checks is the next task, and this is the shape it builds against.
